quickAnswerTitle: Quick Answer: Comfort Colors 1717 vs Gildan 5000?
quickAnswer: Choose Comfort Colors 1717 for premium streetwear and casual luxury: its 6.1 oz heavyweight ringspun cotton, vintage garment-dyed wash, and relaxed boxy drape make it the gold standard for high-end graphic merch. Choose Gildan 5000 for high-volume budget promos: it is significantly cheaper, but features stiff carded cotton that shrinks and fades faster.
intro: Whether you are launching a custom apparel line, printing merchandise, or simply building a rotation of heavy casual blank t-shirts, two heavyweight names dominate the American blank market. Both brands are actually manufactured under the Gildan Activewear parent umbrella, yet they cater to completely different quality tiers and fashion sensibilities. We break down the exact differences between the cult-favorite Comfort Colors 1717 and the mass-market Gildan 5000.

sections.heading: 1. Fabric & Dyeing: Garment Dye vs. Piece Dye
paragraphs: The defining magic of the Comfort Colors 1717 lies in its garment-dye process. The t-shirt is sewn completely from raw cotton and then submerged into specialized dye baths. This yields subtle tonal fading around the seams and guarantees virtually zero shrinkage for the customer.
The Gildan 5000 uses traditional piece-dyeing: the fabric roll is colored before being cut and sewn. The result is a flat, uniform color that lacks the vintage, lived-in aesthetic of Comfort Colors.

sections.heading: 2. Yarn Quality: Ringspun Softness vs. Carded Stiff Cotton
paragraphs: Comfort Colors utilizes 100% ring-spun cotton. The spinning process aligns and twists the individual fibers tightly, producing a smooth, ultra-soft surface that feels substantial at 6.1 ounces per square yard.
The Gildan 5000 uses standard open-end carded cotton (5.3 oz). It feels noticeably stiffer and scratchier out of the package, and the fibers tend to fuzz after multiple wash cycles.

sections.heading: 3. Fit & Silhouette: Streetwear Boxy vs. Boxy Promo
paragraphs: Comfort Colors 1717 features a fashionable relaxed, boxy cut with substantial collar ribbing that does not stretch out. It has become the darling of modern streetwear brands and university merchandise.
Pair a washed pepper Comfort Colors tee with tapered utility trousers. Explore our guide on What Color Shirt with Olive Green Pants for effortless weekend combinations.

faqs.question: Why is Comfort Colors more expensive than Gildan?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors utilizes higher-grade ringspun cotton, complex garment-dyeing techniques, and enzyme pre-washing, which requires specialized processing that adds to production cost.

faqs.question: Does Comfort Colors 1717 shrink in the dryer?
faqs.answer: Virtually zero shrinkage occurs because the garment-dye process preshrinks the fabric during factory production.
